title: Frontend: Lazy Evaluation
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Lazy Evaluation. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({values,take,minimum}). Build a lazy iterable filtering values >= minimum then doubling them; consume at most take outputs. Return {values,visited}, counting only pulled source elements. take is a nonnegative integer; take=0 must visit nothing.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Represent the pipeline as iterable adapters or generator functions for map/filter/take.
alternativeApproaches: Add async iterables with cancellation and bounded prefetch rather than launching every task eagerly.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: No consumption; take zero; short-circuit.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
